newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israel releases detained Lebanese fishermen.
newsitem.headline: Israel releases detained Lebanese fishermen.

text.p: A pro-Syrian Shi'ite Moslem group said on Monday one of its guerrillas destroyed an Israeli gunboat in a dawn suicide attack off south Lebanon, but the Israeli army later denied that the attack had succeeded.
"One of our militants launched a martyrdom attack against a Zionist navy boat near the shore off Tyre and destroyed it," a spokesman in Beirut for Amal, Lebanon's mainstream Shi'ite group, said.
"The claim is false. No Israeli navy ship was sunk," an Israeli army spokesman in Jerusalem responded.

Security sources in Jerusalem said earlier an Israeli patrol boat killed a guerrilla in a fishing boat heading for an attack on Israel. The patrol boat opened fire about two km (one mile) offshore at about 5:30 a.m. (0230 GMT).
An explosion occurred on the fishing boat after it was fired on, the sources said.

"This morning an attempted terrorist attack...was thwarted by a navy boat which was on routine patrol north of Rosh Haniqra (in northern Israel). During the incident a guerrilla was killed," an Israeli army spokesman said.
Lebanese security sources in the southern port of Tyre said Israel released three Lebanese fishermen at 6:00 p.m.(1500 GMT) after detaining them for more than six hours.
Earlier, the Lebanese security sources had said an Israeli naval ship had seized a fishing boat and forced three Lebanese fishermen on board to sail to Israel.
Guerrillas in south Lebanon frequently attack Israeli troops and their local militia allies holding a 15-km (nine mile)-wide border strip in a bid to drive them out of Lebanon.
